# Notebook Practical Operation Entry

This directory contains the accompanying Notebook for the AMD ROCm policy replication project. Sections 01–06 focus on the environment, metrics, and diagnostics; sections 07–13 complete the full execution chain from keyboard data collection, formal training, MuJoCo closed-loop, pi0 strict-input to Pi0.5 EEF-delta/chunk alignment diagnosis; sections 14–16 follow the "one Notebook per model" approach, placing training, long-term training logs, strict evaluations, videos, and conclusions in the same file. The Markdown chapters explain the concepts, evaluation criteria, and experimental conclusions, while the Notebook executes the code line by line, generates configurations, starts tasks, and organizes result tables.

07–16 The output was executed line by line and saved. 07–12 Used the AMD teaching environment; 13 Recomputed tables and images in a isolated Jupyter environment using the same AMD experiment summaries. 14–16 Used the completed model to reconstruct evidence and generate an end-to-end learning interface. Interactive keyboard collection, formal long training, and batch closed-loop processes are still controlled by the `RUN_*` switch. The repository includes path audits, real data summaries, completed training progress, strict success rates, key frames, and four-view videos. These tasks do not start automatically when readers open the Notebook.

It is recommended to start Jupyter from the topic root directory:

```bash
cd /path/to/04-AMD-ROCm策略复刻专题
jupyter lab
```

If it is running on your own AMD device or remote server, set it according to the actual situation first:

```bash
export PROJECT_ROOT=/path/to/every-embodied/mujoco_pnp
export DATA_ROOT=/path/to/datasets/every_embodied
export OUTPUT_ROOT=/path/to/outputs
export MODEL_ROOT="$PROJECT_ROOT/ckpt"
```

When learning from scratch for the first time, the recommended order is `01 → 14`. First, let the learner see the correct behavior of SmolVLA, long training logs, and the strict evaluation criteria, then proceed to `07 → 09 → 11` to collect, train, and evaluate on their own. If you want to understand failure diagnostics, read `15 → 16 → 02/03/05/06`. If there is already data and a checkpoint, you can directly enter the corresponding model from the end-to-end Notebook in 14–16, and then return to 07–13 to review the split sections.

Pre-trained weights, strict evaluation results, and download status can be found in [ Pre-trained Weights and Zero Training Experience ](../08-pre-trained-weights-and-zero-training-experience.md). Historical checkpoints without a public download link should not be included in the run commands; use the built-in videos in the repository first, or train your own verifiable weights.

07 interactive collection and 11 visualization rollout require the available `DISPLAY`; long training from 08–10 requires sufficient model cache, checkpoint space, and stable power supply. All `RUN_*` switches are off by default. Check the commands and paths first, and then turn them on explicitly.

## Re-execution and Acceptance

If the AMD teaching image does not have `jupyter`, `nbclient`, or `ipykernel` installed, a lightweight executor from the repository can be used. It shares namespaces in the order of Notebooks, executes ordinary Python code cells, and writes stdout/stderr back to the standard `.ipynb` outputs; interactive collection and long training are still determined by the switches within the Notebook.

```bash
python code/execute_tutorial_notebooks.py \
  notebooks/07_data_collection_and_audit.ipynb \
  notebooks/08_act_training_rocm.ipynb \
  notebooks/09_smolvla_training_rocm.ipynb \
  notebooks/10_pi0_training_rocm.ipynb \
  notebooks/11_mujoco_closed_loop_deploy.ipynb \
  notebooks/12_pi0_strict_input_end_to_end.ipynb \
  notebooks/13_pi05_random_position_eef_delta.ipynb \
  notebooks/14_smolvla_end_to_end.ipynb \
  notebooks/15_pi0_end_to_end.ipynb \
  notebooks/16_act_end_to_end.ipynb
```

The execution result of the current submission is as follows: 07 corresponds to `11/11` code cells, 08 corresponds to `11/11`, 09 corresponds to `11/11`, 10 corresponds to `12/12`, 11 corresponds to `10/10`, 12 corresponds to `10/10`, and 13 corresponds to `13/13`. In the new end-to-end Notebook, 14 corresponds to `11/11`, 15 corresponds to `9/9`, and 16 corresponds to `9/9`. The public Notebook uses variables such as `$PROJECT_ROOT` to represent machine-related paths, without including remote usernames, private IP addresses, or absolute local directories.
